scope: Secondary closed-loop disturbance study; output has no effect on the frozen primary qualification, training or cost results.
selection: Pin each checkpoint and sequence using its completed primary score before opening disturbance outcomes; record the primary report digest. Declare all selected cases even if the unperturbed policy fails before intervention.
onset: First rising source frame reaching at least 50 percent of peak world-Z object displacement from the original initial pose. Apply during the next two reference intervals whose first frame equals that onset. If peak <20 mm or two intervals are unavailable, intervention is not applicable.
design: For every chosen checkpoint/sequence use two signed wrist-target pulses. Compare a fresh deterministic policy using its actual state observation at each action to open-loop playback of the unperturbed trajectory's saved per-substep finger and wrist commands. Only the wrist position target along world X is disturbed. Per-axis remaining calibrated residual target allowance clips the disturbance; all motor gains and effort limits remain active. Virtual object forces are zero. Neither source nor scene is shifted.
analysis: Each perturbed trajectory compares actual wrist/object displacement to its own mode's unperturbed trajectory on common timestamps. Observe 30 intervals after the pulse, report source pose errors, pre-pulse divergence, applied target deltas, actual observed departures, first subsequent three-frame return within 2 mm and 2 degrees, and any subsequent departures. Unexposed, partially exposed, censored and early terminated cases remain in the assigned denominator. No physical departure is a separate result from recovering after a departure.
